title: Theo and the Terminal
premise: Isandro Montrose, a xenolinguist turned cargo hauler, intercepts a distress call in Vessic — a language extinct since the Meridian Purge two centuries ago. Following it, he finds a hidden enclave of Vessic survivors whose existence was erased from every official record after a corporate-sponsored massacre. To win them justice, Isandro must reconstruct the truth from fragments of speech, forged ledgers, and his own fading dreams, while the corporation's enforcers close in and the enclave's leaders must decide whether exposure means salvation or annihilation. In the end, Isandro broadcasts the reconstructed testimony to every port in contested space at the cost of his ship, his livelihood, and nearly his life — and the survivors, finally named, choose to step into the light rather than vanish again.
about_author: Isandro Eastwick is a former shipping clerk who spent a decade aboard freighters before turning to fiction, and his prose carries the salt-and-rust texture of long-haul space. He writes science fiction about people the galactic record forgot.

chapters.title: Static in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hauling ore through the Kestrel Verge, he decodes an anomalous distress signal and freezes: it's Vessic, a language he studied as a student and that officially has no living speakers. The beat is vertigo — a ghost calling out of the dark.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Cargo
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with flashbacks to his linguistics career collapsing when he began dreaming in alien phonemes instead of English. He debates ignoring the signal; debt and loneliness tip him toward answering. Emotional beat: quiet desperation disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Coordinates That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro triangulates the signal to a rogue moonlet inside a corporate exclusion zone owned by Halcyon Combine. His nav AI flags the route as fatal. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve as he burns toward the forbidden.

chapters.title: First Contact, Second Silence
chapters.summary: Isandro docks at a hollowed asteroid and meets Sera Venn, a Vessic elder who speaks the language fluently — proof of everything history denies. She tests him before trusting him. Beat: wary wonder on both sides.

chapters.title: The Enclave Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Sera leads him through tunnels to a settlement of three hundred Vessic descendants living off scavenged tech. Isandro realizes they are the last of a genocide no one recorded. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: What the Archives Say
chapters.summary: Isandro cross-references official records in his ship's database: the Vessic 'voluntarily relocated' in 2187, population zero by 2190. The lie is seamless. Beat: cold anger at how cleanly erasure was executed.

chapters.title: Sera's Testimony
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She recounts her grandmother's memories of the Purge — the orbital bombardment, the falsified manifests. Isandro records everything. Beat: grief transmitted across generations through voice alone.

chapters.title: A Language Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Isandro discovers why Halcyon erased the Vessic: their homeworld sat atop rare isotopes, and a living claimant culture would void the mining charters. Beat: the machinery of profit revealed behind atrocity.

chapters.title: The Listener Problem
chapters.summary: Isandro explains that testimony alone proves nothing; courts require corroboration, and all witnesses are legally nonexistent. They need physical evidence — the black box of the destroyer Meridian's Wrath. Beat: hope constrained by procedure.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Allies
chapters.summary: Enclave council POV (Doran, Sera's rival). Hardliners want Isandro gone, fearing discovery; moderates back the plan. A knife-edge vote authorizes the salvage mission. Beat: a community arguing about survival versus justice.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessic Again
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Immersed in the enclave, his linguistic gift reawakens — he dreams in Vessic for the first time in twelve years and wakes weeping. Beat: identity healing even as danger grows.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro and young archivist Tey forge shipping credentials to enter Halcyon's scrapyard station where decommissioned warships are stripped. Beat: tension of impostors walking through light.

chapters.title: The Scrapyard of Evidence
chapters.summary: Aboard the gutted hulk of Meridian's Wrath, Isandro locates the black box vault — but finds a Halcyon audit team already aboard, pulling the same records. Beat: race turned standoff.

chapters.title: Two Minutes in the Dark
chapters.summary: Action chapter, Isandro's POV. He kills the station section's power, steals the core, and barely escapes as alarms cascade. First blood on his hands. Beat: adrenaline followed by nausea.

chapters.title: What the Box Remembers
chapters.summary: Decrypted aboard his ship, the black box contains firing orders signed by Halcyon director Cassian Roe himself. Proof exists — but only Isandro knows. Beat: triumph shadowed by target-on-back fear.

chapters.title: The Hunter Assigned
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Warden Ilsa Kreutz, Halcyon's fixer, traces the stolen core to a cargo hauler's transponder. She begins closing the net with methodical patience. Beat: the predator introduced.

chapters.title: Port of Liars
chapters.summary: Isandro stops at freeport Calloway to find a journalist or court willing to hear him. Every advocate he approaches declines within hours — Halcyon's money reaches everywhere. Beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Tey's Gamble
chapters.summary: Tey, having stowed away to help, broadcasts a fragment of the firing order on pirate bands, hoping sympathetic smugglers will spread it. It works — and tells Kreutz exactly where they are. Beat: courage with consequences.

chapters.title: The Net Tightens
chapters.summary: Kreutz's patrol ships lock down Calloway. Isandro hides the core inside a shipment of mourning relics bound for a Vessic memorial barge. Beat: ingenuity under pressure.

chapters.title: Sera Speaks to Strangers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Against council orders she travels to Calloway and gives public testimony in Vessic, untranslated, daring the crowd to dismiss a living witness. Beat: defiance as catharsis.

chapters.title: Riot of Memory
chapters.summary: The freeport erupts — some rally to the Vessic cause, others sell information to Halcyon. Kreutz arrests Sera. Beat: solidarity and betrayal in the same hour.

chapters.title: Bargaining Chips
chapters.summary: Kreutz offers Isandro a trade: the black box for Sera's release and amnesty for the enclave. He sees the trap but cannot refuse outright. Beat: moral weight pressing down.

chapters.title: The Council Divided
chapters.summary: Enclave POV. Doran argues surrendering the core guarantees extinction-by-attrition; Sera, freed by sympathizers, argues silence does too. The community fractures. Beat: justice vs. survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Isandro's Confession
chapters.summary: Isandro admits to Sera that his testimony once helped convict an innocent man early in his career — the sin that ended his academic life. He fears his word is poison. Beat: shame offered like an open wound.

chapters.title: The Third Witness
chapters.summary: Tey discovers a third source: a retired Halcyon archivist, Marta Oyelaran, who kept personal copies of the Purge files out of guilt. Beat: hope arriving from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: Marta's Vault
chapters.summary: Isandro visits Marta on a retirement habitat; she confirms everything but will only testify if guaranteed protection — which requires publicity, which requires risk. Beat: chain of trust being forged link by link.

chapters.title: Kreutz Closes In
chapters.summary: Kreutz's POV. She corners Isandro's ship in open space; a cat-and-mouse chase through a debris field ends with his engines crippled and the core's location compromised. Beat: the walls closing.

chapters.title: The Price of the Core
chapters.summary: To escape, Isandro jettisons his cargo and life savings — twelve years of work burned as decoy mass. He arrives at the enclave with nothing but the truth. Beat: sacrifice made literal.

chapters.title: Doran's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Doran demands Isandro leave and take the fight elsewhere; staying invites extermination. Isandro counters: running is what let Halcyon erase them the first time. Beat: the argument that defines the book.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Plan
chapters.summary: Together they design a single coordinated transmission — black box audio, Marta's documents, Sera's testimony — pushed simultaneously through every relay in contested space so suppression is impossible. Beat: strategy crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Kreutz's Last Offer
chapters.summary: Kreutz infiltrates the enclave alone, offering Doran wealth and legal recognition in exchange for Isandro. Doran's answer — recorded — becomes evidence of Halcyon's ongoing crimes. Beat: temptation refused.

chapters.title: Night Before the Signal
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. The enclave prepares: children taught the words they'll speak, elders polishing relics, Isandro calibrating antennas. Quiet intimacy before the storm. Beat: communal courage.

chapters.title: The Transmission
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The broadcast goes out across forty relays. Halcyon scrambles jamming ships; Kreutz assaults the enclave to seize the source. Beat: the world changing in real time.

chapters.title: Defense of the Enclave
chapters.summary: Battle chapter. Miners, smugglers stirred by the broadcast, and enclave defenders hold the tunnels against Kreutz's troops. Tey is wounded shielding the transmitter. Beat: ordinary people choosing to stand.

chapters.title: Isandro Versus Kreutz
chapters.summary: Personal climax. Isandro confronts Kreutz in the antenna chamber; she offers him his old life back to stop the final relay. He completes the transmission as her soldiers breach. Beat: identity chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The testimony spreads faster than Halcyon can burn it. Ports riot, charters are suspended, and an independent tribunal convenes. Kreutz withdraws, her mandate dead. Beat: exhale after suffocation.

chapters.title: The Tribunal
chapters.summary: Isandro testifies — flawed past and all — alongside Sera and Marta. His old sin is aired and weighed; the tribunal rules the massacre proven and the Vessic a living people. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Halcyon collapses into scandal; compensation flows, but nothing returns the dead. Isandro, penniless and shipless, reckons with whether it was worth it. Sera answers him without words. Beat: melancholy tempered by meaning.

chapters.title: A Name Restored
chapters.summary: The enclave votes to leave hiding, resettling on their chartered homeworld. Doran and Sera reconcile; Tey recovers and becomes the enclave's first licensed archivist. Beat: rebirth of a people.

chapters.title: Dreams in Two Languages
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Isandro's POV. Aboard a new ship crewed by Vessic and humans alike, he dreams again — half English, half Vessic, wholly himself. He sets course for the homeworld. Beat: peace earned, identity whole.
